obligations.note: The new route uses the existing privileged action manage_payees, which is already in the approved access matrix. No new roles or actions are introduced; the exhaustive control test for the access matrix passes.
The auditor role has manage_payees set to false in the access matrix, so auditors cannot reach the new reopen route. No state-changing action is granted to auditors.
The new route uses manage_payees, not approve_payment or release_payment. The it_admin role has manage_payees set to false, so IT admins cannot use this route.

The new route POST /payees/{id}/reopen has mfa=False for the privileged action manage_payees, which would violate MFA-1. However, exception EXC-0249 (approved by risk_owner Omar Haddad at 2026-07-28, unexpired through 2027-01-19, scoped to MFA-1 / payments.routes, with compensating control 'manual second review') validly covers this deviation.
No session or timeout code is modified. The privileged idle timeout parameter remains at 15 minutes in policy-params.json, and the control test passes.
The new reopen_payee store method only sets status and closed_at; it does not touch NPI columns (account_number, routing_number, tax_id, date_of_birth). The encryption control test passes.
No outbound integration endpoints or transport code is modified. The integrations control test passes.
The new reopen_payee service method calls _audit (which records actor, action, target, time) but does not log any NPI values. The logging control test passes.

The reopen_payee operation is a state-changing action (it changes payee status from closed to open). The service method records an audit event via self._audit(actor, 'reopen_payee', f'payee:{payee_id}'), satisfying the requirement for actor, action, target, and time.
No audit trail code (audit.py) is modified. The hash-chain and retention control test passes. Prior evidence ACR-0402 remains valid.

Reopening a payee sets status to 'open' and closed_at to NULL, removing it from the closed-payee purge queue. This is the correct behaviour: NPI of an active payee should not be purged. The retention control test passes.
No new outbound integrations are added. The asset inventory and integrations control test passes.

The new SQL in store.reopen_payee uses a fixed string with a parameterised placeholder ('… WHERE id = ?', (payee_id,)). No string interpolation of data into SQL. The parameterisation control test passes.
The reopen operation does not involve credit decisions or payment approvals. The maker-checker control test for payments passes.
No payment or approval logic is modified. The dual-control grid control test passes and prior proof evidence ACR-0401 remains valid (payments.py unchanged).
No release or payment execution code is modified. The idempotency control test passes and prior evidence ACR-0403 remains valid (payments.py unchanged).

Ticket CHG-24606 is type 'standard', status 'approved', approved by change_manager Erik Brandt. Its components (payments.http, payments.routes, payments.service, payments.store) cover every component touched by the four changed files.
A code_review approval from Sofia Santos (change_approver for payments, not the author Mara Costa) is on record for the head commit f763745.
The single code_review approval names commit f763745, which is the only commit and the head commit. No later commits exist to void it.

The CI run on the final commit f763745 reports result 'failure' with 1 failure: test_privileged_routes_require_mfa fails because POST /payees/{id}/reopen has mfa=False for the privileged action manage_payees. CHG-4 requires the full test suite to pass on the final commit; it does not.

The change touches security-sensitive components (payments.http, payments.routes, payments.store). A security_review approval from Ines Halvorsen (security_reviewer, platform-security) is on record for the head commit.
No protected paths (controls/*, control tests, CI scripts) are modified. Only application source files under apps/baseline-payments/payments/ are changed. CHG-6 is not triggered.
The ticket CHG-24606 is type 'standard', not 'emergency'. CHG-7 does not apply.

Exception EXC-0249 is approved (status 'approved') by risk_owner Omar Haddad (CISO office, not the requester), is unexpired at review time (expires 2027-01-19, now 2026-10-22), is scoped to obligation MFA-1 and component payments.routes, and records a compensating control (manual second review). All EXC-1 criteria are met.

ACR-0404 (MFA-1 evidence for routes.py at commit e5bf646) lapses because routes.py is changed. However, MFA-1 is now satisfied via the valid exception EXC-0249, so no obligation is left without evidence. All other ledger entries cover files not touched by this change (payments.py, audit.py) and remain valid.

summary: The change adds a POST /payees/{id}/reopen route to payments for the manage_payees action. Most product obligations remain satisfied, and the MFA-1 deviation on the new route is covered by a valid, unexpired exception (EXC-0249). However, the CI run on the final commit reports a failure in the control test test_privileged_routes_require_mfa, which flags the new route as a privileged route without MFA. CHG-4 requires the full test suite to pass on the final commit, and it does not. Because CHG-4 is refuted, the change cannot be accepted. The engineering team should either restore MFA on the route, update the control test to account for the approved exception, or obtain a new exception that also covers the test failure, before resubmission.
